note: Compatibility rules for the Mr. Backup Z64. Every entry names the source it came from. Titles are matched by distinctive substring against the release name, so a key must be specific enough not to collide with a different game in the same series.

unit.memory_source: Official manual, September 1998, feature list: in-built 256Mbit memory
unit.larger_titles_note: Support for 512 Mbit titles appears in the BIOS 2.18 release notes as planned and never delivered, so a larger ROM cannot be loaded from disk under any BIOS.
unit.extension_source: Tables read from the unit's own menu binary after decompression
unit.unsupported_note: The little endian form is absent from the extension table, so convert such a dump to big endian before use.

6102.note: The common case, and the chip a standard boot cartridge carries.

6103.note: Set Boot Chip to 6103 in Game Setup.

6105.note: Emulated at about 99 percent. Country Fix and Slow Down must both be off.

6106.note: Set Boot Chip to 6106 in Game Setup.

boot_cartridge.requirement: A cartridge carrying a 4 KB EEPROM save chip and a 6102 or 7101 security chip.
boot_cartridge.source: Unit FAQ, entry on boot cartridges: as standard boot cart you should use Super Mario 64 or any other cart with a 4KB eeprom savechip and a 6102/7101 security chip
boot_cartridge.note: Together with boot chip emulation and the country fix, this boots almost every title.

donor_source: Unit FAQ, entry on boot cartridges, which lists the titles each save cartridge serves

one_save_per_cartridge.source: Unit FAQ: you can only save on game's savegame on a single cart. To save more than one game you need multiple save carts
one_save_per_cartridge.consequence: Keeping progress in several unemulated-save titles at once needs one donor cartridge per title.

will_not_boot_without_donor.title: Mario Party 3
will_not_boot_without_donor.source: Unit FAQ: Mario Party 3 doesn't even boot without a 16Kb eeprom boot cart like SW Racer

oversized_titles.title: Ogre Battle 64 - Person of Lordly Caliber

oversized_note: Measured from a public release set. The tool also flags any scanned ROM above the memory limit, so this list is a convenience rather than the authority.
